main_text.p: Ϛiov Crassi non erat ex omni parte militibus munitum. Figuram ejus supra posuimus. Πλινθίον est igitur quod Græci παλινδ̀ ita vocarunt, quod ἐπ πεζαγώνῳ χήμαῖ fingitur, quam etiam πεζάγωνον πᾶξιν appellant, & πεζάπλευρον quod in omni latere quadrati dispositos haberet milites contra hostem obversos, quæ ibi vocatur σωπαξις ὁπλιτῶν πεζαγωνῳ, & sic describitur: λέγεται αὐτὴ καὶ ᾧ ᾧ τῆς παλαιὰς πεζάπλευρον, ἔχουσα καθ' ἕκαστον μέρος ἀνὰ ᾧ ᾧ γῶν τεσσάρων ὡς εἶναι ἑωὶ ᾧ τ ποσάρων πλευρῶν ᾧ ᾧ δώδεκα. Dicitur hoc genus instructionis quadrata apud veteres, etiam quadrilaterum, quod in omni parte tres habet acies directas, ut in totum per quatuor latera duodena habeantur acies instructæ. Nam πεζαγώνῳ & πεζάπλευρα τάξεως, quadratæ simul & quadrilateræ instructionis hæc erat forma.

page.notes: The diagram is a square formation: outer P labels along the four sides (top three, bottom three, left two, right two), inner E labels along an inner square around a central box marked I. The Greek passage is partly illegible and transcribed approximately; Greek letters with accents and breathings may be inexact. Faint marks at the page edges and the watermark-like text at bottom right are not printed text.
